note: Progress measures functional equivalence with OSRS through implementation tasks: done counts fully, in progress counts halfway, and to do counts zero. Automated test coverage is evidence, not a scoring requirement. Reconciled against tsps main 3e9ee2d67 on 11 November 2026, covering 1,355 merged PRs since the 6 November checkpoint 3b61a15a8. This sync credits the implemented portions of Clan Wars, Burthorpe Games Room, ranked PvP Arena, Trouble Brewing, Intelligence Gathering, Halloween, seasonal rares, Brutus and Maggot King. It also records Hunter Rumours, diary and League task updates, Sailing, bank-funded Grand Exchange offers, Curse of the Empty Lord, quest progression fixes, combat and interface work. Existing inventory, task scope and weights are retained. Only merged main changes are credited.

item: weight? (optional, default 1, 0 = listed but not counted)

instructions: Each item inherits its category taskTemplate only when it has no taskDetails; every item here ships explicit taskDetails, so read those first.
Replace nothing: the plugin path is the file to create or extend, implementedIn lists what already exists, and refs link the wiki page/section and real source lines to copy from.
Follow server/AGENTS.md: plugin-first, name-based hooks, handlers outside register, cross-plugin talk via onCustomEvent/emitCustomEvent.

Resolve ids from the cache/generated identifiers, never bare numbers. Generated osrsreboxed JSON must only change through source/parser fixes and regeneration in ../osrsreboxed-db; use the established plugin-owned data sources for plugin data.
Status values are todo, in-progress and done. Progress is derived automatically; never enter a percentage.

categories.name: Core engine
categories.summary: Shared systems that all game content runs on.

taskTemplate.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Trace every caller and lifecycle hook for {feature} and record the authoritative entry point (the matching phase in World.process in game/World.ts, or GameEngine.run) only where it is non-obvious.

State the valid inputs, owned state and observable outputs for {feature}; reuse the nearest existing engine service (World, TaskManager, PlayerSession, PlayerPersistence) instead of adding a parallel manager.
Keep feature logic out of PluginManager: cross-plugin behaviour goes through api.emitCustomEvent("domain:event", payload) / api.onCustomEvent as defined in plugins/PluginTypes.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: All callers route through one authoritative implementation.
Invalid state is rejected without corrupting world, player or plugin state.

taskTemplate.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Connect {feature} to startup/tick/login-logout/shutdown only where its state actually changes: GameBuilder.initialize() starts the loop, GameEngine.run() ticks, Server.gracefulShutdown() drains.
Make repeated initialisation and cleanup idempotent (guard flags already used by PluginManager.loadFromDirectory and GameEngine.tickInProgress).
Ensure a thrown handler cannot orphan a registration, timer, queued Task or world entity; per-entity work is wrapped and fails that entity only.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting and stopping the server twice produces the same registered state.
An interrupted {feature} operation cleans up every resource it owns.

taskTemplate.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Identify which {feature} state must survive logout or restart and put it in PlayerSave, registered with PlayerSave.persistAttribute(key) (surfaced to plugins as api.persistAttribute).
Validate and default missing or stale values in PlayerSave.applyToPlayer; never replay transient runtime state from before logout.
Restore state before dependent packets or plugins consume it (applyToPlayer runs in NetworkBuilder.enterWorld before the handshake is sent).
acceptanceCriteria: Old saves without the new fields still load.
A save/load round trip preserves all player-visible {feature} state.

taskTemplate.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: List the tick-order, disconnect, duplicate-request and capacity edge cases for {feature}, using the World.process phase order as the ordering contract.
Add guards at the shared mutation boundary (for example the queue drain in World.process or ClientConnection.handle) rather than at each caller.
Make failures observable with an actionable log or player message, and request that one entity logout instead of corrupting the tick.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate or reordered requests cannot duplicate state or items.
Disconnecting mid-operation leaves the world and persistence consistent.

items.name: Movement & pathfinding
devNotes: Implemented: NetworkBuilder.walk() (net/NetworkBuilder.ts:861) turns a MOVE_GAMECLICK into MovementQueue.requestWalk() with the run flag, and MovementQueue.process() consumes one queued step per 600ms tick from Player.process (game/entity/impl/player/Player.ts:413) and NPC.process.

Implemented: tile clipping is RegionManager.canMove/canMovestart over the pinned flag constants; route selection is PathFinder.calculateRoute -> RsmodRouteFinding.findRoute, and walkToTile/walkToEntity/walkToObject/walkToGroundItem queue TaskType.WALK_TO work drained by TaskManager.processRemainingWalkTo().

Missing: deterministic coverage. package.json declares test:pathfinding, test:combat-pathing and test:route-core, but server/scripts/{pathfinding,combat-pathing,rsmod-route-core}-smoke.ts are absent in this checkout, so no smoke script exercises clipping, diagonal pillars, follow repath or walk-to today.

PR #283 (f4131ce7): walkToEntity is now a pursuit - Player.process calls MovementQueue.processEntityPursuit before the movement phase; it tries the interaction before stepping and re-paths to the target's current tile when points.length <= 1 or the route was invalidated, so a moving NPC is not trailed and the op resolves on the arrival tick. server/tests/npc-exact-move.test.cjs covers the occupancy rules.
PR #360 (3eaeeb6c): the energy threshold to re-enable running (setting 389, varbit 11031) works as captured, only after run naturally depletes.
Main 281766303 (2 November 2026): #1686 keeps walking through partial animation stalls; #1767/#1801 restore minimap click routing; #1925 fixes following persistence and stop conditions.

Main 0a219d100 (2026-11-03): #1949 turns frozen players towards an out-of-range clicked target without moving them. #1898 measures an exact move’s completion from the current tile; existing ordinary-world movement credit is retained.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document that MovementQueue owns per-Mobile queued points, run toggle, pursuit checkpoint and destination flag; the only client entry is NetworkBuilder.walk(), and ticks drive it via Player.process/movement and NPC.process.

Enumerate the public surface: requestWalk, addSteps, walkToTile/walkToEntity/walkToObject/walkToGroundItem, setPursuitCheckpoint, beginCycle, and the outputs didMoveThisCycle, wasBlockedByDynamicOccupancy, wasRouteInvalidated, hasPendingWork.

Keep collision lookups in RegionManager.canMove/canMovestart; path-blocked notifications go through PluginManager.emitPathBlocked (plugins/PluginManager.ts:773) so plugins never re-implement tile math.
acceptanceCriteria: Every movement path (click, follow, walk-to, NPC retreat) funnels through MovementQueue.process().
No plugin duplicates RegionManager tile/collision logic.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Queue steps only during packet handling; drain exactly one step per tick inside MovementQueue.process(), reached from Player.process (movement phase) and NPC.process, never concurrently from World.process.
Make RegionManager.init() + MovementQueue.handleRegionChange() idempotent so a scene rebuild resets the queue (MovementQueue.reset) without orphaning a WALK_TO Task.
On logout/disconnect reset the queue and cancel WALK_TO work via TaskManager.cancelTasks(key) so a stale route cannot survive the session.
acceptanceCriteria: A player who logs out mid-walk leaves no queued steps or WALK_TO task behind.
Repeated region loads do not duplicate or drop movement state.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Persist only durable movement inputs (run toggle and run energy) through PlayerSave; the saved tile and orientation are already serialized in PlayerSave.
On hydration (PlayerSave.applyToPlayer, PlayerSave.ts:643) clear the movement queue and force needsPlacement so a pre-logout route is never resumed.
Do not persist transient route state (pursuit checkpoint, stepBlocked flags, lastSentDest); rebuild it from the first post-login tick.
acceptanceCriteria: Login restores the saved tile and run state but never resumes a pre-logout path.
Missing or stale saved position fields default to GameConstants.DEFAULT_LOCATION.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Guard the shared mutation boundary: MovementQueue.beginCycle() runs once per tick and duplicate requestWalk/addSteps within a tick coalesce rather than appending past MAXIMUM_SIZE (100).

Use wasBlockedByDynamicOccupancy plus the lastSentDestX/Y de-duplication so a dynamically blocked actor re-evaluates instead of emitting path_blocked every tick (PathFinder debounce, PathFinder.ts:14).
When a forced movement or teleport is applied (ForceMovementTask, teleportation model) clear the queue before writing the new tile.
acceptanceCriteria: Two clicks on the same tick produce one route, not two.
A disconnect during forced movement cannot leave the actor registered on a stale tile.

items.name: World tick & lifecycle
devNotes: Implemented: GameEngine.init()/run() schedules a 600ms setTimeout loop (GameConstants.GAME_ENGINE_PROCESSING_CYCLE_RATE), skips overlapping ticks via tickInProgress, measures drift/overrun and calls World.process(); GameBuilder.initialize() wires Systems.init, RegionManager.init, the startup definition loaders and PluginManager.emitServerStartup.

Implemented: World.process() (game/World.ts:979) runs the ordered phases — TaskManager, ItemOnGroundManager, add/remove player and NPC queues, active-NPC and player processing, walk-to sweep, HitQueue.processAll, update buckets, visibility, PlayerSession.flush, resetUpdating — and Server.gracefulShutdown emits shutdown then World.savePlayers() + GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.flush().
Missing: no deterministic lifecycle/restart test and no periodic autosave phase; task 5 is todo. The loop is single-threaded Node with a self-correcting setTimeout, not a fixed-rate interval.

PR #871 measures gameplay cooldowns in game ticks across combat, skills, items, minigames and NPCs, avoiding real-time timer drift. This strengthens already-complete lifecycle criteria without adding score.

Main 8403b60db (4 November 2026): #2049, #2116, #2182 — Special-attack dead clicks and hit-time dialogue interruption are repaired. Death removes earlier-life PvP damage while legitimate queued Vengeance/reflected damage still receives capped kill credit.

Main 3b61a15a8 (6 November 2026): #2356 Add configurable cross-floor visibility and combat; #2379 Fix Castle Wars practice bot patrols and flag runs. Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.

Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #4381 Settings: Ctrl-clicks on NPCs, objects, ground items and players invert the run mode. #3836 World config page: edit world settings from a local admin page (v0.1). #2731 Per-server character slots: one login, several characters, a picker after login.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document the authoritative loop: GameEngine.run() calls World.process() once per 600ms cycle and nothing else may tick world state.

List the World.process phase order (task_manager, ground_items, queue_add/remove, process_npcs, process_players, walk_to_sweep, combat_hits, rebuild_update_buckets, update_players_npcs, flush_network_players, reset_player_updates, reset_npcs) as the ordering contract content relies on.
State that World owns players/npcs/objects/ground-item collections and queued add/remove lists; GameEngine owns only scheduling and diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: All per-tick state mutation happens inside World.process under one call stack.
No second scheduler or interval mutates world collections.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Keep GameBuilder.initialize() the single startup path: Systems.init (NPC implementations), RegionManager.init, loadStartupData, new GameEngine().init(), then PluginManager.emitServerStartup.
Make the setTimeout scheduler unref() and re-arm from the measured drift so a slow tick does not compound (GameEngine.scheduleNextRun / logTickLag).
On shutdown emit PluginManager.emitServerShutdown, World.savePlayers and await PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.flush before process.exit, as Server.gracefulShutdown already does.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling initialize twice registers systems once and starts one loop.
SIGINT/SIGTERM persists players before exit and does not double-run the shutdown.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Tick state (processCycle, activeRegionIndex, update buckets, combatActiveNpcs) is runtime-only and must not be serialized; document that in the process() header.
Durable state is reached through World.savePlayers() -> GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.save(player); ensure the shutdown path flushes async backends via PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.flush().
After a restart rebuild region/active-region state from RegionManager.init and NpcSpawnDefinitionLoader rather than from any saved snapshot.
acceptanceCriteria: A restart with an old save set preserves player-visible state and rebuilds world state deterministically.
No transient tick counters appear in PlayerSave.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Rely on the tickInProgress guard plus logOverlap to prevent re-entrant ticks, and logTickOverrun/FreezeDiagnostics for stalls rather than blocking the loop.
Bound queue draining with GameConstants.QUEUED_LOOP_THRESHOLD (150) so a burst of logins cannot starve a tick; a disconnect mid-tick is caught per player and turned into requestLogout().
Catch per-phase exceptions (World.process wraps TaskManager, ground items, player processing and flush) so one bad entity does not abort the whole tick.
acceptanceCriteria: A thrown entity process lowers to a logout for that entity and the remaining phases still run.
Adding/removing many players in one cycle completes within the queue threshold.

items.name: Player and NPC synchronisation
devNotes: Main 62d662706: #1431 attack animations no longer stall for most weapons; some weapons still need their own patches.

PlayerUpdateDecoder now queues a teleport before a forced move in the same player update (covered by player-sync-teleport-force-move.test.ts); NPC timer hitpoints/headbar/XP scaling widened the wire for Gemstone Crab and is covered by its test.

PR #702 (a1c53188): World enforces the 255-actor caps on retained and newly added views, rejects duplicate actors and stale references after world-slot reuse, and filters private instances before applying the nearby-player budget. NPCs respect owner-only boat visibility; a full NPC view reserves a slot for the owner's eligible pet without moving it between instances. Existing PlayerSession backpressure closes remain in place, with regression coverage for pressure that builds before the microtask flush.

PR #221 (29f698d0): Mobile.showHitsplat shows display-only hitsplats that change no hitpoints, with a cache hitsplat id for the target and another for observers plus an optional health bar; HitDamage carries the ids and PlayerSession writes them. Wintertodt's warmth meter uses it.

PR #271 (af45cdff): HitQueue.process applies every hit due on a tick via Mobile.addTickHit; SINGLE_HIT/DOUBLE_HIT are replaced by one Flag.HIT and PlayerSession.createActorUpdates sends the full Mobile.getTickHits list, so multi-hit attacks show every splat on the landing tick (post-lethal hits as 0).

PR #277 (eb469454): HitDamage carries a source and PlayerSession.hitView gives the dealer their own bright hitsplat for hits they dealt; CombatFactory.applyResolvedHitDamage and the specials set the attacker as source.

PR #283 (f4131ce7): a priority-1 animation (seq config opcode 10, skilling loops) requested on a tick the player stepped is held one cycle and applied on the next non-moving tick (Player.performAnimation + NpcAnimationScanner.getSequencePriority), matching the client's p_arrivedelay; server/tests/arrival-animation.test.cjs covers held vs immediate play.

A map rebuild restores the normal scene after instance exit. #2222 removes human block-animation fallbacks for unknown creature rigs.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document that PlayerSession owns the per-session sync cursors (PlayerSyncState, NpcSyncState, sceneBaseX/Y, appearanceCache) and that Player owns the local player/NPC lists refreshed by World.
Reference the ClientProtocol.ts types (PlayerView, NpcView, ActorUpdateView, PlayerSyncState) as the wire contract and keep field order owned by encodeServerPacket.
State the one-way flow: World builds local lists -> PlayerSession.flushClient encodes -> BinaryChannel sends; nothing may send PLAYER_SYNC/NPC_INFO outside flushClient.
acceptanceCriteria: All sync packets originate from PlayerSession.flushClient.
The wire field order matches the ClientProtocol types.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Flush only after every observer has built its frame for the tick: World.process runs update_players_npcs before flush_network_players, then reset_player_updates/reset_npcs.
On login force a full appearance/placement refresh (NetworkBuilder.enterWorld flags Flag.APPEARANCE and Mobile.setNeedsPlacement) so the first flushClient sends a complete baseline.
Skip non-network actors: World.shouldRunNetworkUpdates excludes player bots and disconnected sessions from both visibility work and flush.
acceptanceCriteria: A freshly logged-in player receives a complete baseline scene and actor set.
Bots never receive or trigger sync work.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Sync state is session-only: PlayerSyncState/NpcSyncState, scene base and appearanceCache are rebuilt per login and must not be serialized in PlayerSave.
On reconnect, reset PlayerSession cursors (setPlayer) and re-send appearance so no diff is computed against a foreign session's baseline.
Persist the underlying actor state (location, appearance, equipment) through PlayerSave; sync simply renders it next tick.
acceptanceCriteria: Reconnecting with an existing save produces a correct baseline with no ghost actors.
No sync cursor fields appear in PlayerSave.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Keep the local-list caps and resize behaviour (MAX_LOCAL_PLAYERS, MAX_NEW_LOCAL_PLAYERS_PER_CYCLE, resizeViewDistance) when adding/removing actors mid-cycle so a crowded tile cannot overflow the 255-slot view.

Reject duplicate actors and stale references after world-slot reuse; filter private instances before the nearby-player budget. World.updateLocalNpcs applies BoatManager.syncArea/canSeeAboard and isOwnerOnly/getOwner, reserving a slot for the owner's eligible pet without changing its area.
Treat backpressure as a disconnect: PlayerSession.flushClient checks OUTBOUND_WS_BUFFER_CRITICAL_BYTES and closeBackpressuredWebSocket rather than buffering unbounded.
acceptanceCriteria: A player entering a crowded area never gets more than the configured local caps.
Instance/private-area players never see each other's actors, and a backpressured socket closes instead of growing without bound.

items.name: Accounts & sessions
devNotes: Implemented: NetworkBuilder.ClientConnection.login/enterWorld/cleanup (net/NetworkBuilder.ts:720) validate revision against CachePipeline.getActive().revision, reserve ClientConnection.pendingNames against simultaneous logins, check PlayerPunishment.banned/IPBanned, load the save through GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE, apply it with PlayerSave.applyToPlayer, emit PluginManager.emitPlayerLogin and send the handshake.

Implemented: cleanup on socket_close/socket_error/logout closes the channel, releases the pending name and queues removal; World's remove queue honours canLogout/forcedLogoutTimer, and a duplicate login kicks the existing copy via existingPlayer.requestLogout() (game/World.ts:1010).

Task 4 guards are in place: PR #239 (c18d6a68) stops a socket closed during the async password check from staging a pending login, refuses a queued handshake on a closed connection, releases the reserved name, and wraps World/MobileList removal hooks so one throwing logout/save hook cannot abort the tick; covered by server/tests/core-disconnect-guards.test.cjs. login-protocol-harness.ts remains the runnable protocol check and ban lists come from PlayerPunishment.init (server/data).

Main 3b61a15a8 (6 November 2026): #2191 Fix worn DFS and tentacle options unequipping the item (#2165); #2330 fix: handle Monster Inspect casts on NPCs; #2356 Add configurable cross-floor visibility and combat; #2614 Match OSRS beginner combat damage and default new accounts to Punch. Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.
Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #2859 Fix ban, mute and IP moderation commands.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document that ClientConnection owns the pending login (PendingLogin), the reserved name and the resulting Player for one socket, and that PlayerSession is the socket's writer via setPlayer.

State the login flow contract: decode LOGIN -> validate -> PlayerPersistence.load -> hash/check password -> pending -> LOGIN_RESPONSE; HANDSHAKE/enterWorld -> new Player + World.add + emitPlayerLogin.
Confirm failure codes map onto net/login/LoginResponses.ts and failLogin, so responses are not hand-rolled per branch.
acceptanceCriteria: One socket yields at most one Player and one reserved name at a time.
Every login failure returns a code from LoginResponses with a player-visible message.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Reserve the lowered name in ClientConnection.pendingNames for the whole login, and release it in releasePendingName on every exit path (success, failure, socket close).
enterWorld creates PlayerSession, applies the save, adds to World, emits PluginManager.emitPlayerLogin with isNewAccount, then sends handshake/animations/gameframe.
On cleanup, guard against double invocation (this.player / closed) and make the logout path send encodeLogoutResponse, flushPackets, then close.
acceptanceCriteria: A failed login never blocks that username from retrying.
Socket close and explicit logout both release exactly one name and queue one removal.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Load through GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.load(username) and hydrate via PlayerSave.applyToPlayer before the handshake; set rights/developer override and password hash on the Player.
Support password migration: accept a legacy plaintext match, otherwise GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.checkPassword, and re-encrypt via encryptPassword on the next save.
New accounts (pending.save == null) get defaults from PlayerSave and DEFAULT_LOCATION; the isNewAccount flag lets plugins grant starters.
acceptanceCriteria: Save/load round trip restores position, skills, inventory and plugin attributes.
A legacy plaintext password still logs in and is upgraded on save.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Prevent simultaneous/duplicate login with the pendingNames set plus World.getPlayerByName and an addPlayerQueue scan (NetworkBuilder.login), returning the already-logged-in code.
Handle mid-login disconnect: release the reserved name and null the pending blob; if the load or hash throws, failLogin(8) rather than leaking the reservation.
Honour forced logout and world updates: World's remove queue removes on disconnected || canLogout || forcedLogoutTimer.finished() || Server.isUpdating().
acceptanceCriteria: Two sockets racing the same username produce one login and one rejection.
A disconnect during login leaves no reserved name and no half-built Player in World.

items.name: Save persistence
devNotes: Implemented: abstract PlayerPersistence.load/save/exists/flush plus encryptPassword/checkPassword (game/entity/impl/player/persistence/PlayerPersistence.ts); GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE defaults to NullPlayerPersistence until a plugin calls api.setPlayerPersistence (plugins/PluginManager.ts:3240).

Implemented backends: SqlitePlayerPersistence (node:sqlite, WAL, player_saves table), JsonPlayerPersistence (atomic write + directory fsync) and IndexedDbPlayerPersistence (browser host, PBKDF2 hashing); PlayerSave serializes skills, inventory/equipment/bank, varps, and plugin attributes via PlayerSave.persistAttribute(key) / api.persistAttribute.

Missing: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md claims a 120s bulk save via savePlayers(), but no autosave timer exists — World.savePlayers() only runs on shutdown and after a failed tick. Task 4 (async/flush concurrency) is in-progress and task 5 is todo.

PR #404 (e7801c37): Autosave.plugin.js saves every online player every 15 minutes (staggered, max 10 per tick), SIGHUP saves and exits, and the SQLite backend keeps gzipped save history with ::snapshots/::rollback and yarn saves:rollback.

Main 8403b60db (4 November 2026): #2063, #2179, #2182 — Captured auxiliary quest varbits and saved no-jaw appearance survive login; death/respawn separates stale damage from legitimate reflected kill credit.

Main 3b61a15a8 (6 November 2026): #2356 Add configurable cross-floor visibility and combat; #2379 Fix Castle Wars practice bot patrols and flag runs; #2614 Match OSRS beginner combat damage and default new accounts to Punch. Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.

Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #3948 Hardcore Worlds: world type, Death's Office start, death choice, Escape crystal. #3415 Use world.json name for branding and pre-login metadata. #2731 Per-server character slots: one login, several characters, a picker after login.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document the PlayerPersistence contract (load, save, exists, optional async flush, encryptPassword, checkPassword) and that GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE is the single mutable holder.
Define PlayerSave as the serialized shape; plugin state is opt-in via PlayerSave.persistAttribute(key) exposed as api.persistAttribute (PluginManager.ts:3239).
State that the backend is chosen by a persistence plugin at load time through api.setPlayerPersistence and core code never imports a concrete backend.
acceptanceCriteria: Only one active PlayerPersistence instance at a time.
Core code paths call GameConstants.PLAYER_PERSISTENCE rather than a concrete class.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Save on logout and shutdown through World.savePlayers() -> PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.save(player), and await PLAYER_PERSISTENCE.flush() in Server.gracefulShutdown before exit.
Load in NetworkBuilder.login and apply via PlayerSave.applyToPlayer in enterWorld; keep the new-account default path when load returns null.
Plugins self-register their backend in register(api) with api.setPlayerPersistence(new Backend()), guarding against double registration.
acceptanceCriteria: Logout persists immediately and shutdown flushes every pending write.
Swapping backends needs no core change, only a plugin registering a different instance.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Register every plugin-owned field with PlayerSave.persistAttribute(key) and read it back through Player.getAttribute/setAttribute in PlayerSave.applyToPlayer (PlayerSave.ts:709).
Default or drop stale/missing values during hydration so older saves load; the legacy JSON import path (PLAYER_SAVE_IMPORT_LEGACY_JSON) is opt-in only.
Write attributes only for keys registered as persistent (PlayerSave.cloneAttribute) to keep saves small and avoid leaking transient runtime objects.
acceptanceCriteria: Old saves without a newly registered attribute still load and default cleanly.
A save/load round trip preserves every persisted attribute exactly.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Make save safe against overlapping writes: Json serializes through atomic temp-file + fsync, Sqlite relies on WAL and busy_timeout, and flush() drains async work before shutdown.
Guard save during disconnect: World.savePlayers skips players with the botSkipPersistence attribute, and the remove queue saves orphaned in-combat players before removal.
Ensure flush() is called after the last save on shutdown so a promise-based backend cannot lose the final snapshot.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent save and shutdown cannot corrupt or truncate a save file/database.
A disconnected orphan is persisted exactly once before removal.

items.name: Plugin runtime
devNotes: Implemented: PluginManager.loadFromDirectory (plugins/PluginManager.ts:439) discovers *.plugin.js depth-first, filters names disabled in world.json, resolves dependencies via loadPluginCandidatesWithDependencies and skips bots/PlayerBots under --disablePlayerBots.

Implemented: attach-only register() and the typed hook surface in PluginTypes.ts; executeHook isolates and profiles each handler; the only cross-plugin channel is emitCustomEvent/onCustomEvent (PluginManager.ts:729); registerCommand rights-check centrally via PluginManager.commandRights; registerContentEndpoint -> ContentApi.register and registerCustomInterface -> CustomInterfaceRegistry.register.

Missing: deterministic coverage of load ordering/disabled filtering. package.json declares test:plugin-config but server/scripts/plugin-config-smoke.ts is absent in this checkout; task 5 is in-progress.

PR #594: world.json plugin on/off maps merge with deployment overrides, plugins can default to disabled, unknown names warn, and legacy disabledPlugins remains backward compatible. Achievement plugins move under plugins/achievements/ with source references updated.

(7 merged PRs touch the recorded implementation; highlights shown.) Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document the plugin module contract from AGENTS.md: module.exports = { name, register(api) }, register is attach-only and handlers are module-scope named functions.

Reference plugins/PluginTypes.ts as the authoritative hook list (onObjectInteraction, onNpcInteraction, onItemAction, onPlayerProcess, onPlayerLogin, onCustomEvent, registerCommand, registerContentEndpoint, registerCustomInterface, persistAttribute, getTaskManager, getObjectManager, getWorld).
State that PluginManager holds generic hook plumbing only; feature behaviour must not add new PluginManager methods (use custom events).
acceptanceCriteria: Every plugin exports one name and an attach-only register.
No feature-specific method is added to PluginManager.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: Keep PluginManager.loadFromDirectory the single load point, called from Server.main before GameBuilder.initialize (Server.ts:211), so hooks exist before the first tick.

Fire lifecycle emissions from the engine: emitServerStartup/emitServerShutdown (GameBuilder, Server.gracefulShutdown), emitPlayerLogin/Logout/Disconnect (NetworkBuilder, World), and emitPlayerProcess from World.process.
Resolve inter-plugin load order with loadPluginCandidatesWithDependencies and make loadFromDirectory idempotent via its initialized flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling loadFromDirectory twice loads the plugin set once.
Startup/shutdown hooks fire exactly once per server lifecycle.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Plugin-owned persistent state must call api.persistAttribute(key) (PluginManager.ts:3239 -> PlayerSave.persistAttribute) and read/write through Player.getAttribute/setAttribute.

Server-defined interfaces and content endpoints are read-only public resources served via registerCustomInterface/registerContentEndpoint (GET /api/interfaces/<groupId>, /api/<name>) and must not carry player state.
Validate and default plugin attributes during PlayerSave.applyToPlayer so removing a plugin does not break loading older characters.
acceptanceCriteria: A plugin attribute survives a save/load round trip.
Unregistered or removed plugin attributes are ignored rather than fatal on hydration.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Rely on executeHook to catch and log a throwing handler so one plugin cannot abort a tick or another plugin's handler.
Keep emitCustomEvent synchronous and fire-and-forget: the emitter owns the payload shape and reads the mutated reply immediately after (AGENTS.md cross-plugin rule).
Reject invalid registrations at the boundary: unknown/minimum rights are normalised, invalid content endpoints are caught, and disabled names are normalised before filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: A throwing plugin handler leaves the world tick running.
A custom event with no listeners is a no-op and never throws.

items.name: Networking & packets
devNotes: Implemented: NetworkBuilder.initialize binds the WebSocket server on NetworkConstants.WEBSOCKET_PORT (or BrowserHostHttpBridge for the browser host); ClientConnection.handle decodes with decodeClientPackets then dispatches every ClientMessage type (move, npc_option, object_option, widget_action, trade_action, ...). A per-connection input Promise serializes handle() calls so packets from one socket never interleave.

Implemented: ClientProtocol.decodeClientPackets/decodeClientPacket/encodeServerPacket own opcode lengths and field order (ClientPackets/NativeClientPackets/ServerPackets); PlayerSession.sendClientPacket batches frames up to MAX_GAME_MESSAGE_BYTES and enforces NetworkConstants.OUTBOUND_WS_BUFFER_CRITICAL_BYTES backpressure, sending via BinaryChannel / DataChannelBinaryChannel (WebRTC).
Note: there is no MessageRouter or ActionScheduler class in this repo despite docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; routing is the switch in NetworkBuilder.handle and the listeners under net/packet/impl.

PR #702 (a1c53188): ClientConnection enforces a 64 KiB incoming-message limit and PACKET_QUEUE_LIMIT (240) queued frames while an earlier handler awaits persistence. Malformed or overloaded connections close, release reserved login names and discard queued input; disconnect removal and save requests continue if trade cleanup throws. server/tests/core-disconnect-guards.test.cjs covers real WebSocket fragmentation, coalesced input ordering, backlog limits, login cleanup and outbound batch/backpressure guards. Validation included 196 server tests, six client test files and a five-second live sample with 300 headless load players; manual browser playthrough was not performed.

PR #239 (c18d6a68): server/tests/core-disconnect-guards.test.cjs covers malformed frames, the backpressure close, local view caps and the login/disconnect race; removal hooks are wrapped so one throwing hook cannot abort the tick.

Dedicated relay worlds (c59ac9e8): WebRtcGameConnector advertises WORLD_WEBSOCKET_URL in its relay directory entry and fails session-open with "websocket_required" when it is set, so gameplay runs on the dedicated ws/wss endpoint while the relay keeps player counts.

Dedicated relay worlds (c59ac9e8): WebSocketBinaryChannel.remoteAddress trusts x-real-ip only when the socket address is loopback and the value passes net.isIP (core-disconnect-guards.test.cjs covers it); client discovery swaps the relay url for the advertised ws endpoint in relayWorldEntries/resolveServerTransport before any ICE/TURN request.

PR #737 (7776b149): game packets queue per connection and run at the start of the player's turn (PlayerSession.processPackets), so eating, equipping, prayers and interface actions land on the next tick as live; connection upkeep, login, free movement and logout stay immediate.

Main 0a219d100 (2026-11-03): #1939 preserves WebRTC guests through login-time data-channel drops and reconnect handling. #1973 compresses dense map-region replacements so editor saves fit their network payload. #1898 sends the map clock and an explicit server logout notification.

Main 8403b60db (4 November 2026): #1974, #2045, #2060, #2212 — Official-client target/modal/clan resync, chatbox trade acceptance and IF1 close buttons are repaired; superseded input prompts release their pending answers.

Main 3b61a15a8 (6 November 2026): #2191 Fix worn DFS and tentacle options unequipping the item (#2165); #2301 fix: serve registered content on dedicated WebRTC channels; #2330 fix: handle Monster Inspect casts on NPCs; #2356 Add configurable cross-floor visibility and combat; #2380 fix: use the correct action verb in shared creation menus; #2399 Use the native OSRS quest list and repair quest state publication. Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.
Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #4125 List settings-derived tags for standalone worlds. #3415 Use world.json name for branding and pre-login metadata.

taskDetails.name: Define the runtime contract and ownership
steps: Document the layering: BinaryChannel (ws or WebRTC DataChannel) carries bytes, ClientProtocol owns encode/decode and opcode lengths, ClientConnection.handle owns dispatch, PlayerSession owns outbound batching.

List the ClientMessage union from ClientProtocol.ts as the dispatch contract; supported opcodes without a typed handler decode to { type: "raw" }, while unsupported opcodes and truncated packets are rejected at the boundary.
State that clients never send JSON at runtime; all server writes go through encodeServerPacket/PacketSender and all reads through decodeClientPackets.
acceptanceCriteria: One class owns decode, one owns dispatch, one owns outbound batching.
No runtime JSON crosses the game socket.

taskDetails.name: Implement lifecycle integration
steps: On connection send the welcome with GameConstants.GAME_ENGINE_PROCESSING_CYCLE_RATE and arm onData/onError/onClose handlers (NetworkBuilder.ClientConnection constructor).
Drive login -> handshake -> enterWorld -> logout through the same handle switch, and on close/error call cleanup then queue removal.
Keep PlayerSession the only outbound path for a logged-in player: World.process calls player.getSession().flush(cycle) after visibility updates.
acceptanceCriteria: A socket that closes before login releases its reserved name and never creates a Player.
A logged-in player's packets flush once per tick through PlayerSession.

taskDetails.name: Persist and restore state
steps: Networking state is session-only: PlayerSession scene base, appearance cache and sync cursors reset on each connection and are never written to PlayerSave.
Per-login security state (ISAAC seed via net/security/IsaacRandom.ts) is re-established at login and discarded on close.
The only durable data crossing the socket is player state already covered by PlayerSave; packets themselves are never persisted.
acceptanceCriteria: Reconnecting creates fresh session cursors with no cross-session leakage.
No packet or cursor state appears in PlayerSave.

taskDetails.name: Handle tick-order and disconnect edge cases
steps: Reject malformed frames at the boundary: decodeClientPackets throws on unsupported opcodes or truncated lengths and ClientConnection logs, cleans up and closes the channel so later frames cannot continue a malformed session.

Let WebSocket reassemble transport fragments and decode coalesced packets in order through the per-connection input Promise chain. Bound incoming messages to MAX_GAME_MESSAGE_BYTES (64 KiB) and queued frames to PACKET_QUEUE_LIMIT (240); on overflow release pending login names and discard queued input.
Apply outbound backpressure: PlayerSession closes the channel at OUTBOUND_WS_BUFFER_CRITICAL_BYTES and coalesces synchronous interface packets into one browser message.
acceptanceCriteria: A malformed or split frame cannot crash the server or desync a session.
A slow client is closed rather than growing the outbound buffer without bound.

taskTemplate.name: Register quest state and requirements

acceptanceCriteria: Every registered stage has a reachable dialogue entrypoint.
Repeating or cancelling dialogue cannot skip objectives or duplicate rewards.

taskTemplate.name: Implement objectives and world interactions

Validate prerequisite stage and required items at the shared handler before advancing.
acceptanceCriteria: Objectives cannot be completed out of order.
Quest-only items can be recovered and are cleaned up when appropriate.

taskTemplate.name: Implement journal, rewards and completion

acceptanceCriteria: The completion scroll and quest list update immediately.
Completion is idempotent and rewards cannot be claimed twice.

devNotes: Synced with tsps main e811aff0c (15 October 2026): Registered quest stages, transcript dialogue handlers, world objectives, journal and once-only completion rewards are implemented in the current quest module.
Quest objectives remain partial where the module documents substituted puzzles, travel, followers or encounters; completion alone is not treated as full OSRS equivalence.

Documented implementation limits: - There is no Sailing API in api.core, so Will and Anne's ship and the raft are approximated. items.name: Death to the Dorgeshuun
devNotes: Main 4b1eac7f6: #1249 Kazgar's and Mistag's recorded quick travel through the tunnels. Fix to credited content.

Synced with tsps main e811aff0c (15 October 2026): Registered quest stages, transcript dialogue handlers, world objectives, journal and once-only completion rewards are implemented in the current quest module.
Quest objectives remain partial where the module documents substituted puzzles, travel, followers or encounters; completion alone is not treated as full OSRS equivalence.

Documented implementation limits: - Zanik does not truly follow: the plugin moves her to the player's side at every scripted interaction, zone entry and login (the static cellar Zanik 4507 is the varp-794 transform that appears at stage 1). - The optional tour stops (the tutors, Fred, Millie, Father Urhney, the candle seller, Gee/Donie, the border guard) are not implemented; only the five stops the transcript gates on (Duke, a common man/woman, Father Aereck, goblins, the shopkeeper) plus Cook, Hans, Bob, the Guide, Mistag and Kazgar. - The Tears of Guthix collection minigame is skipped: Juna's dialogue hands the sequence straight to the twenty-tears cutscene. - The water mill tunnel, both quest trapdoors and the working drilling machine are runtime objects registered by this plugin, because the cache maps place only the broken machine. Smashing deregisters the working model and reveals the static broken one. - The store-room guard sequence is one talk-to snipe per guard instead of the full patrol/line-of-sight puzzle; the agility crack and lock doors keep their 23 Agility / Thieving checks. - No Sigmund prayer switching; the cellar Sigmund is the level-50 cache NPC (991) and dies to ordinary combat. The three henchmen are optional. - Followers/pets are always allowed, so the transcript's pet condition answers false; there is no light-source requirement in the caves, and the end-of-quest torch is only granted when the player carries no light.

Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #4276 Death to the Dorgeshuun: Fred, the candle seller and the Al Kharid border guards join the Lumbridge tour. #4093 Fix quest progression, temple repair, and bone shortbow combat. #3796 Fix quest interactions, passage routing and Fishing Trawler recovery. 4 merged PRs changed recorded implementation files for this entry.

items.name: The Giant Dwarf
devNotes: Synced with tsps main e811aff0c (15 October 2026): Registered quest stages, transcript dialogue handlers, world objectives, journal and once-only completion rewards are implemented in the current quest module.
Quest objectives remain partial where the module documents substituted puzzles, travel, followers or encounters; completion alone is not treated as full OSRS equivalence.

Documented implementation limits: - Telekinetic Grab on a ground item cannot be hooked in this server and Dromund is static, so both boot pickups use a 50% "he is not looking" roll (retry if he spots you). The right boot's Take replays the transcript's Telekinetic Grab branches; the cat branch (6GAow8) is unreachable and answers false. - The consortium loop tracks one pinned company and one task at a time, with no delivery timer or per-company score; +20 per ore delivery, +12 per bar delivery, -2 for cancelling, +20 once for the Purple Pewter H.A.M. headstart. - Cutscene room availability is always "a room is available"; optional scenes are played as transcript lines, with no camera or statue swaps. The boatman's post-quest Travel option is not handled. - The "[company name]" placeholder in spoken lines is filled, but option labels are not routed through the line hook, so the one option reading "Yes! Long live the [company name]!" keeps its wiki placeholder.

Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #4351 The Giant Dwarf: answer the return-to-Keldagrim step by its current id. #3796 Fix quest interactions, passage routing and Fishing Trawler recovery. #3567 Keep Giant Dwarf consortium progress by company.

devNotes: Synced with tsps main e811aff0c (15 October 2026): Registered quest stages, transcript dialogue handlers, world objectives, journal and once-only completion rewards are implemented in the current quest module.
Quest objectives remain partial where the module documents substituted puzzles, travel, followers or encounters; completion alone is not treated as full OSRS equivalence.

Historical implementation limits from the October checkpoint (superseded where later notes record fixes): - The ship battle area is static here, not instanced: sailing teleports to the battle map deck (1815,4837 plane 1), and the end cutscene teleports to Mos Le'Harmless (3665,2982) instead of playing scenes. - Climbing nets (11244/11310) are not in Ladders.plugin.js, so this plugin moves the player between deck and mast top on their Climb options. - The rope swing is the wiki's use-rope-on-hoisted-sail with a 42 Agility gate; a failed swing plays the fall variant and drains run energy, and the success lands on the other ship's deck directly rather than via a net. - Plunder containers respawn after 15 s (wiki: up to 5 minutes); logging out respawns them, which is honoured on the login bootstrap. - The fire roll uses the wiki's Ranged-scaled hit chance for both the canister and cannonball shots, so a miss has to be cleaned and reloaded. - Lighting the fuse always succeeds with a tinderbox (the "fuse refuses to light" variant is unreachable); a bullseye lantern is refused, per the wiki. - The dump's empty-store branch reads "You have plunder to deposit." devNotes: Synced with tsps main e811aff0c (15 October 2026): Registered quest stages, transcript dialogue handlers, world objectives, journal and once-only completion rewards are implemented in the current quest module.
Quest objectives remain partial where the module documents substituted puzzles, travel, followers or encounters; completion alone is not treated as full OSRS equivalence.

Historical implementation limits from the October checkpoint (superseded where later notes record fixes): - The Meiyerditch rooftop maze is approximated. The route objects that are placed (pots/door key, wall ladders, locked shortcut door, rocky surface, barricade, ladder repair) are wired where the cache places them, but the rooftop jumps, crawl walls, tightropes and push-walls are not simulated; the barricade opens straight onto the Drakan walls. The old diary/bed beat is skipped: this cache revision has no bed transcript object and no old diary item. - The vyrewatch do not patrol or notice the player; the "being noticed" encounter plays on Talk-to during the contact phase. The tithe costs 6 hitpoints, fighting only damages and ends the chat (no mine punishment), and the distraction succeeds deterministically at 40+ Thieving. - The Meiyerditch mine punishment ("Send me to the mines!") is not implemented; its transcripts are marked unavailable in the dump. Daeyalt ore and the mine cart exist but are not part of the verifier route. - The fireplace only has Look-at on the cache object; the knife/sickle interactions are item-on-object. The inner laboratory door is a state check rather than a real door swap, and the laboratory stairs teleport. - Sketches need the player near the marked approach (north 3556,3379, west 3522,3357, south 3572,3331); a short guidance line is sent when using charcoal on papyrus away from all three (the wiki page has no line for that case). - The quest's skill requirements (Construction 5, Mining 20, Thieving 22, Agility 26, Crafting 32, Magic 33, Strength 40) are not enforced, matching the other quest plugins. Only In Aid of the Myreque completion gates the start, so the shared Veliaf is not stolen from that quest. - The post-quest shortcut doors and the tome's three 2,000 XP charges are not simulated; the tome is handed over as the 3-charge item.

Main 281766303 (2 November 2026): #1690 adds stage/item guards, the sickle-symbol rooftop route, item recovery and Vanstrom's five-hit ambush. Objectives remain partial for non-patrolling Vyrewatch, the absent mine punishment and documented substituted interactions.

Documented implementation limits: - The jester control-panel interface does not exist here, so the two performances play the wiki's instruction/overheard-plans/success lines as chained cutscenes (mawnis-instructions + honour-guard + friedleif plans + after-a-successful-performance) and always succeed; the -again variants that only "jump above" reuse the first performance's lines. - King Sorvott, Mawnis, Kjedelig and Trogen are played through this plugin's own Talk-to interception because their quest variants are not indexed to their NPC ids; their post-quest own-page dialogues still play when this plugin returns no variant (indexed NPCs only). - The window/beard tax's number-entry step is absent, so the "right amount" condition is answered true and the too low/high ones false. - The tax bag is tracked in the persisted "quest.the_fremennik_isles.tax" attribute and mirrored onto the 5 cache tax bag items (0/10k/20k/29k thresholds); its Check option prints the exact wiki line. - Thorkel's alternative ore hand-in (starting-off-ore-delivery-talking-to- thorkel) is not wired to consume ore; the King's hand-in is the path. - The Ice Troll King (5822) has no spawn in npc-spawns.json: he is spawned owner-only south of the cave bridge once the player has killed 10 frenzied trolls, at (2392,10244,1) (the lair tiles across the bridge); the head is granted on his death rather than cut from a corpse object (21622 is not placed in this cache). - Bridges keep their broken appearance after Repair (the swap object has no placement here); clicking Walk-across on a repaired bridge moves the player over it. acceptanceCriteria: A match starts and ends once under normal and cancellation paths.

acceptanceCriteria: Scores visible to clients match authoritative server state.

acceptanceCriteria: All documented arena routes and interactables have a handler.

taskDetails.name: Entry, lobby and team rules
steps: Add the Barbarian Outpost ladder and a five-slot lobby where Commander Connad assigns a role; reject a role whose wiki prerequisites the player does not meet.

Two consecutive runs must start at wave 1 with fresh penance and no double-awarded Honour points.
acceptanceCriteria: A match starts and ends once under normal, dropped-team and cancellation paths.
A second match begins at wave 1 with an empty arena and no inherited timers.

Known differences retained in the implementation: no play-time eligibility gate, all server worlds permit BH, binds are cleared on the next arena tick rather than prevented, and matchmaking/exit timings include documented estimates. The three-way retaliation case has a regression test but has not been visually replayed.

Fur tier controls the Crafting XP (base 1,560 plus the fur's Hunter XP value), and a fast shaping rhythm reduces each side from 20 to 15 ticks. Read the exact tables from the wiki.

taskDetails.name: Implement entry, lobby and team rules
steps: Add the sunstone rocks, monolith, plinths and Auchrie NPCs with their object ids and tiles from the wiki and cache.
Record the 60 Crafting requirement and the chisel/hammer/four-sunstone cost.
acceptanceCriteria: Every plinth and rock resolves to one interaction; the level and cost match the wiki.

taskDetails.name: Implement the match state machine
steps: Implement mining sunstone with momentum, carving each of the four sides and inserting a sunstone core plus fur to finish a golem.
Award Crafting XP and Hunter XP for the fur according to the wiki table, including the tick-perfect shaping speed-up.
acceptanceCriteria: A golem cannot be finished with a missing side/core/fur; XP matches the fur tier used.

taskDetails.name: Implement objectives, scoring and rewards
steps: Open the golem crafting interface/overlay, show carving progress and play the chisel/hammer/finish animations.
Give the uncut gemstone reward and close the plinth state when the golem is complete.
acceptanceCriteria: The four sides show progress and the completed golem disappears into the reward.

taskDetails.name: Implement arena mechanics and cleanup
steps: Handle logout mid-carving, a full inventory and two players using the same plinth.
Reset an abandoned plinth and persist nothing that would duplicate the one-time unlock.
acceptanceCriteria: Relogin cannot complete a golem without the materials; plinths do not stay stuck.

Gwenith Glide's out-of-bounds edge is estimated and the Stormy key has no chest yet (docs/barracuda-trials.md).
Completion always grants Sailing XP; first-time rank targets grant keys, ship facilities and fabric rolls. Read the time limits, facilities and locations from the wiki.

Define the Swordfish/Shark/Marlin rank time limits and collection objectives.

taskDetails.name: Implement the match state machine
steps: Implement the timed skiff obstacle course, trial-specific objectives and rank completion.
Track fastest times and unlocked ranks per player; a non-skiff boat cannot start.
acceptanceCriteria: A completed run awards the correct rank/XP; a wrong boat or missing facility is refused.

taskDetails.name: Implement objectives, scoring and rewards

Show the scoreboard and rank feedback.

Do not award a rank if the player did not finish the trial objectives.

items.name: Rat Pits
devNotes: Greenfield cat-vs-rat minigame: four pits (Ardougne kitten, Varrock cat, Keldagrim overgrown cat, Port Sarim wily cat), unlocked through Ratcatchers and barred to Ironmen.
Two players bet 100-20,000 coins, choose a cat strategy with a catspeak amulet, and the winning cat takes the pot and growth time. Ratcatchers is implemented, but the pits are not.

Gate each pit on partial Ratcatchers completion and record the 100-20,000 coin bet range.
acceptanceCriteria: Each pit only accepts its required cat type and the correct quest stage.

steps: Implement two-player betting, cat strategy selection with a catspeak amulet, the rat fight and win/loss/draw.
Advance cat growth by the wiki amounts for Ardougne/Varrock and handle a cat death or run-away.
acceptanceCriteria: Both bets must match before the fight; the winner receives the pot and the documented growth.

Show the required cat type and the player's cat state in the interface.

taskDetails.name: Implement arena mechanics and cleanup

items.name: Tears of Guthix
devNotes: Implemented across server/plugins/minigames/tearsofguthix/: Juna's quest/cooldown/admission checks, the private timed cave with bowl and drifting streams, the light-creature sapphire-lantern crossing, south rocks, diary bonus/PB and cleanup on every exit path.

PR #885 (49e14c389) completes the weekly UTC cooldown, QP/100k XP eligibility, journal/reminder, concurrent private visits, exact QP countdown, stream sequence and lantern travel; the quest itself remains in TearsOfGuthix.Quest.js.
Limits: exact carry duration/landing visuals and gaps between stream moves are documented estimates; no browser animation/overlay capture was made.

Main 3e9ee2d67 (11 November 2026) changes touching recorded implementation: #4093 Fix quest progression, temple repair, and bone shortbow combat. #3735 Tears of Guthix: Sailing only after Pandemonium is complete.

taskDetails.name: Entry, weekly timer and eligibility
steps: Gate entry on the quest completion flag plus the seven-day cooldown, resetting at the start of the 7th day after the last completion and requiring at least 100,000 total XP or 1 quest point earned since; surface the remaining days and the QP/XP requirement in the Quest Journal as the wiki describes.
Only one player participates at a time, so create a per-player instance/PrivateArea (like Barrows) and require the stone bowl in hand (two free hands) before entering.
Persist lastPlayed with api.persistAttribute so the cooldown is correct after logout and restart.
acceptanceCriteria: A player cannot re-enter before the weekly reset and the journal shows days plus QP/XP needed.
Logging out and back in mid-cooldown does not bypass the timer.

taskDetails.name: Core collection loop and mechanics
steps: Build the nine weeping walls with three blue and three green streams active; each stream holds for 16 ticks (9.6 seconds) then moves in a fixed per-world sequence that the client can observe.
Set the time limit to one game tick per quest point and tick the instance from World.getProcessCycle(); collecting blue tears increments the bowl while green tears reduce it.
Auto-remove the player and end the run when the timer expires; leaving through death before the timer ends allows a retry because the minigame deals no damage.
acceptanceCriteria: Blue tears add and green tears subtract exactly once per collection and the run always terminates at the tick limit.
The stream sequence is fixed for the world instance rather than re-rolled per tick.

taskDetails.name: Rewards, XP formula and diary bonus
steps: On exit, award XP in the lowest-XP eligible skill; per-tear XP is min(60, 10 + 110*floor(currentXP/27)) so it caps at 60 per tear from level 30 upward, and the hard Lumbridge & Draynor Diary adds 10%.
Honour the wiki tie-break skill order when several skills share the lowest XP and skip skills whose unlock (Rune Mysteries, Druidic Ritual, a house) is missing.
Grant the XP exactly once per run and record the personal best for the interface as the wiki describes.
acceptanceCriteria: XP lands in the lowest eligible skill and the diary 10% is applied once when unlocked.
A second completion in the same day is blocked and cannot double-grant XP.

taskDetails.name: Persistence, reset and cleanup
steps: Persist only the last-completion timestamp and personal best; destroy the PrivateArea and remove all temporary walls/objects on exit, death, logout, disconnect and shutdown.
Reset the instance timer and bowl state every run so two consecutive runs never inherit tears.
Ensure the stone bowl is returned or preserved as documented and a disconnect mid-instance cannot strand the player in the Chasm.
acceptanceCriteria: Every exit path restores the player and removes the instance.
No temporary wall/object or timer survives a restart.

items.name: Blast Furnace
devNotes: Main 62d662706: #1488 belt, water, sink and dispenser feedback from captures.
Main 688f96a69: #1427 the belt refuses loads while 28 bars wait, conveyor loads save apart from the pot, and the captured dispenser messages.

Implemented in server/plugins/minigames/BlastFurnace.plugin.js and blastfurnace/Machinery.BlastFurnace.js: coffer/HUD, foreman permit, conveyor, half-coal smelting, guaranteed iron, goldsmith XP, cooling/ice gloves, dispenser, manual stove/pump/pedals/pipe repairs, heat/fuel, contribution XP and the coal-bag two-click workflow.

PR #887 (05a2ca195) adds manual and dwarf-operated worlds, machinery repairs, heat/temperature, coke fuel, pedal/pump XP, lead/cupronickel recipes and the coal-bag path; tests cover paid and manual operation, F2P gates and shared cooling.
Remaining source limits: manual heat/fuel/break-chance values and some belt/dispenser timings are explicit estimates; Dumpy's cycle is captured but some Numpty/Thumpy repair triggers remain unknown.

Main 3b61a15a8 (6 November 2026): #2706 Allow reaching the Dwarven Boatman before starting The Giant Dwarf. Existing completion credit and documented limitations are retained unless explicitly updated below.

taskDetails.name: Entry, coffer and dedicated worlds
steps: Reuse the existing coffer, foreman permit and Keldagrim/Rellekka access handlers.
The Giant Dwarf start requirement is enforced at Keldagrim city and Blast Furnace entry; retain coffer/permit checks and keep manual and dwarf-operated worlds distinct through the world zone tag.
acceptanceCriteria: The coffer debit matches the documented fee and an empty coffer blocks smelting with a clear message.
Normal and dedicated worlds behave differently only in who runs the furnace, not in bar cost.

taskDetails.name: Core smelting loop and mechanics
steps: Use the ore/coal conveyor, bar dispenser and pump/bellows; manual worlds own the shared stove/pump/pedals/repairs in blastfurnace/Machinery.BlastFurnace.js.

Reuse Smithing.plugin.js's level checks and SMELTING_INTERVAL_TICKS for the per-bar cadence, but keep the furnace heat, conveyor contents and dispenser queue as shared world state owned by one task rather than per-player state.
Consume run energy while running ore to the conveyor and bars to the bank; stamina potions (custom-shops.json Potion Shop, id 3) are the standard consumable.
Keep the manual machinery mode and coal-bag two-click workflow; retain the dwarf-operated conveyor/smelting loop.
acceptanceCriteria: Coal counts, level checks and XP match a normal furnace except for the halved coal and guaranteed iron.
The shared furnace never produces duplicate bars when two players smelt concurrently.

taskDetails.name: Bars, XP and points
steps: Award Smithing XP per bar on the smelting interval and grant the bars to the dispenser owner exactly once.
Handle a full inventory by leaving bars in the dispenser rather than deleting them.
Persist no bar progress beyond the dispenser; the reward is the bars and the XP.
acceptanceCriteria: Each bar yields exactly one XP grant and one item, never both duplicated.
A full inventory leaves bars in the dispenser with a message.

taskDetails.name: Persistence, reset and cleanup
steps: Persist the coffer balance per player with api.persistAttribute; the shared furnace heat, conveyor and dispenser contents are ephemeral and reset on restart.
On shutdown clear the conveyor/dispenser queues and remove any spawned NPC workers so a restart starts clean.
Destroy any temporary furnace objects/overlays on every exit path.
acceptanceCriteria: Coffer balance survives logout while furnace contents do not persist.
No orphaned worker NPC or queue survives a restart.

Leaving or disconnecting cannot strand minigame-only items or state.
